notes:
I can't give you any notes on Hosea 14 yet, because my research didn't get through. I tried to load five verse-by-verse sources, but I hit a bug in my own code before any page text came back, and then the tool stopped me from making more research calls this turn. The five sources were:

- https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-14/
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/hosea/14.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/hosea/14.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/hosea/14.htm
- https://www.preceptaustin.org/hosea-14-commentary

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written verse notes from memory, because they would look sourced when they aren't.

**What I'd do next (if you send a short follow-up like "continue"):**

1. **Traditional reading:** read the five pages above in full and write notes for v. 1–9, each with its URL.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** search the tradition sites on the main points:
   - v. 2, "fruit of our lips" and its link to Hebrews 13:15 (spurgeon.org, desiringgod.org, ligonier.org, lcms.org, wesley.nnu.edu for Wesley's notes).
   - v. 4, "I will heal their apostasy; I will freely love them": grace and backsliding, which may show a Reformed vs. Wesleyan difference on whether a believer can fall away.
   - v. 5, "dew," sometimes read as the Holy Spirit (enduringword.com, ag.org, samstorms.org).
   - v. 8, the evergreen cypress.
3. **Other views:**
   - Modern scholarship: netbible.org's translator's notes (for example, the textual point in v. 2 about "bulls"/"fruit") and bibleodyssey.org.
   - Catholic and Orthodox: newadvent.org (Church Fathers and the Catholic Encyclopedia), catholic.com and oca.org, since Hosea 14 is read in the Orthodox lectionary.
   - Prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace: I'll only include these if a page on the allowed sites actually discusses them in connection with this chapter.

I'll leave out anything I can't find, as you asked.
